decision_reason: This is CSI Piemonte's specific URL-shortening REST API, not merely a government user of third-party software. The public consortium's source identifies CSI Piemonte, Regione Piemonte, and Città Metropolitana di Torino as copyright owners; a live Regione Piemonte emergency-maps page still uses the exact url-s.it/us/{id} route documented by the source. Its quiet code history is supported by current agency use and direct source-to-service route correspondence.

government_provenance.note: The first-party copyright file names CSI-Piemonte, Regione Piemonte, and Città Metropolitana di Torino (2017–2020); the first-party README describes CSI's own Urlshortner API and deployment. CSI's governance page (https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/chi-siamo/azienda/governance) identifies CSI as a consortium whose members and assembly are public entities, including Regione Piemonte, Città di Torino, and Città Metropolitana di Torino. This is public-body authorship/stewardship, not inferred from catalog usage.

public_source.note: The first-party public repository contains the REST API implementation, schema/deployment instructions, README, publiccode.yml, copyright notice, and full license text without credentials. The README identifies the canonical route and host used by the deployed service.

eligible_license.note: The source README explicitly states EUPL-1.2-or-later and the root License.txt is the EUPL v1.2 text. This grant is scoped to the first-party urlshrtapi source; its PostgreSQL and proprietary JBoss EAP runtime dependencies keep separate terms and are not included in the software-source grant.

primary_evidence.note: Regione Piemonte's live Protection Civil maps page calls the listed URLs permanent map links into its regional Geoportal and includes multiple http://www.url-s.it/us/{id} links (for example http://www.url-s.it/us/cb3d4a37). That exact host/path is the response example in this API's README; on 2026-09-29 the cited short link returned an HTTP 303 to the region's live Geoportal map. The page supplies public user guidance and documents an operational government service; this also establishes current use/source correspondence for the quiet 2020 repository.

product_identity: CSI Piemonte Urlshortner API (urlshrtapi), a REST service that creates and resolves short links used by Piemonte public-service sites
agency: CSI Piemonte (public consortium; first-party copyright also names Regione Piemonte and Città Metropolitana di Torino)
license: EUPL-1.2-or-later for the first-party urlshrtapi source; runtime dependencies are separately licensed
family_note: The scope is the short-link REST API at url-s.it, not the underlying Geoportal/map applications. The assigned repository's README and live Regione Piemonte route provide the source-to-service mapping. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: The first grant-bearing public repository commit is 2020-05-04 and added the license/metadata; the publiccode releaseDate is not used as the source year. Although the repository has not been pushed since 2020, current Regione Piemonte public maps still link through the matching url-s.it/us route, and a cited route returned a live redirect on 2026-09-29. This satisfies the maintained-source exception with direct correspondence evidence.

decision_reason: CSI Piemonte created VIDE and Agenzia Piemonte Lavoro documents actual 2024 public-service use, but the assigned repository is an umbrella documentation/API-spec repository rather than a complete licensed application source. Its README requires separate appschedweb and vide-pwa code and configures a REST API backend whose implementation/canonical repository and grant could not be located; the quiet frontend/source-family mapping to the 2024 service also remains unverified. Hold until the complete deployed-source boundary and rights are established.

government_provenance.note: CSI Piemonte's own product page says CSI developed VIDE, describes it as a service for public administrations, and says it is operated as a service on its certified regional Nivola cloud. CSI's governance page (https://www.csipiemonte.it/it/chi-siamo/azienda/governance) documents its public-consortium structure and public owners. This is product-specific CSI authorship/stewardship, not merely a public agency using a vendor's tool.

public_source.note: The public umbrella repository contains product docs, a Swagger specification, and source links, but its README says the deployed system comprises separate https://github.com/csipiemonte/appschedweb and https://github.com/csipiemonte/vide-pwa components plus a REST API whose implementation is not linked. appschedweb's README config requires VIDE_BASE_URL_API; the root holds only the API specification. The public GitHub organization has no clearly identified VIDE API source repo, so accessible code for the full deployed service is not established.

eligible_license.note: The umbrella README declares GPL-3.0-or-later for its own repository/specification; the separate appschedweb README separately declares GPL-3.0-or-later and has full GPLv3 text, while vide-pwa's LICENSE explicitly grants EUPL-1.2-or-later. Those are distinct component grants and do not establish the rights for the required REST API backend; Jitsi and other dependencies are outside those grants. Product-level license scope is unresolved.

primary_evidence.note: Agenzia Piemonte Lavoro's 2024-10-03 service notice documents a live SOS Curriculum public employment service using Virtual Desk (VIDE) for appointment booking and video consultations; its 2025 activity plan continues to identify the applicative Virtual Desk–Vide for remote services. CSI's product page provides user workflow documentation. This is named public-service use, not the provenance basis.

product_identity: VIDE (Your Virtual Desk), CSI Piemonte's multi-component public-administration appointment and virtual-counter application, comprising appschedweb, vide-pwa and a required REST API service
agency: CSI Piemonte (developer/steward); Agenzia Piemonte Lavoro / Regione Piemonte (documented service operator/user)
license: Unresolved product-wide: umbrella README and appschedweb declare GPL-3.0-or-later; vide-pwa separately grants EUPL-1.2-or-later; source/grant for the required REST API backend not located
family_note: The assigned vide repository is not the whole software family. Its README lists appschedweb and vide-pwa as separate repos and says API services are required; appschedweb configs require a separately hosted VIDE API. The current service is documented by CSI/Agenzia Piemonte Lavoro, but the complete code/deployment map and API rights remain open. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: The root LICENSE-bearing commit dates 2020-10-27; component repos also have first public grants in 2020 (appschedweb GPL-3.0-or-later, vide-pwa EUPL-1.2-or-later). Do not use metadata releaseDate as source year. The root was last pushed 2023-01-13, vide-pwa 2023-01-11, and appschedweb 2020-12-18; despite primary 2024 service evidence, the quiet components and unresolved API source prevent confirming current source correspondence and product-wide licensing.

decision_reason: GeoCity is a vendor-owned third-party product used and customized by public bodies; no product-specific public authorship, commissioning of the canonical product source, public funding, or public stewardship was established. The public agency evidence supports use only, which is not government provenance under the intake rules.

government_provenance.note: The source README states that CST Sistemi Sud S.r.l. owns the product copyright and GeoSafety S.r.l. maintains it. The product catalog and public-body records document public-sector adoption/trial, not public creation or funding of the canonical GeoCity product. A Consorzio di Bonifica di Paestum record describes a GeoCity demo and later customization for its needs; that does not establish public provenance for the vendor's general product/repository. Public-code metadata and AgID design alignment are leads/standards, not authorship evidence.

public_source.note: The canonical public GitHub repository contains the GeoCity source, README with installation requirements and build/publication instructions, publiccode.yml, license text, and a version 1.0.0 product description; no credentials are needed.

eligible_license.note: The root contains the full EUPL v1.2 text; first-party publiccode.yml identifies EUPL-1.2, and the README identifies CST Sistemi Sud as the copyright holder. This grant is limited to the first-party GeoCity source in the repository; Esri, Microsoft, and listed third-party libraries have separate terms.

primary_evidence.note: The Consorzio's own 2024 deliberation documents use of GeoCity in a 2022 water-channel funding application and a 2023 demo, plus a decision to customize the platform for its needs. This is product-specific public-sector use and the repo has a release/install guide, but this source is historical; the repository's last substantive push was 2024-08-12 and no current agency use or source-to-current-service mapping was found, so the freshness baseline remains unresolved.

product_identity: GeoCity, CST Sistemi Sud's commercial GIS/web mapping platform for territorial and municipal information management
agency: No government product sponsor identified; copyright owner CST Sistemi Sud S.r.l.; maintainer GeoSafety S.r.l.; public-sector adopters include Consorzio di Bonifica di Paestum and municipalities
geography: Italy; vendor origin in Campania, with reported use by Italian public bodies
license: EUPL-1.2 for first-party GeoCity repository source; third-party Esri/Microsoft software and dependencies are separately licensed
family_note: Repository README identifies release 1.0.0, gives install/build instructions and names CST as rights owner and GeoSafety as maintainer; publiccode says EUPL-1.2, but its releaseDate is not used as source year. Government records show use/pilot/customization, not sponsor rights over the generic product. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: The assigned canonical repo was created in 2022; its first root LICENSE commit is 2022-08-05, the basis for the first defensible public licensed-source year. Last code push was 2024-08-12 (over 24 months before review); official agency evidence located documents a 2022/2023 use/demo, not continued current operation. Rejected for lack of public provenance regardless of the unresolved freshness check.

decision_reason: NAPS2 is an independently authored and actively distributed document-scanning application, but the French SILL entry is only a government-use/recommendation lead. No government body created, commissioned, funded, sponsored, or stewards this specific product/source.

government_provenance.note: The first-party project identifies NAPS2 as a contributor-developed scanner application and the official site identifies Ben Olden-Cooligan as copyright holder. No public-agency origin, contract, funding, or stewardship for NAPS2 or this source was found. The assigned SILL record is a public-sector discovery/use lead, not evidence that government created or sponsored the product.

public_source.note: This is the current canonical source repository linked by naps2.com, with build instructions, documentation, project structure, source, releases, and accessible issue/release history. The official download page links directly to the source and binaries.

eligible_license.note: The root grant explicitly states GPL version 2 or (at the recipient's option) any later version for the NAPS2 application. The README separately identifies LGPL-2.1-or-later alternatives for NAPS2.Escl, Images, Internals and SDK projects, and MIT for SDK samples; external repositories/dependencies retain their own grants. The application scope is OSI-approved GPL-2.0-or-later.

primary_evidence.note: The current first-party distribution page offers Windows/macOS/Linux installers and version 8.3.2, updated 2026-07-22, with links to documentation, changelog, older releases and source; it reports over 16 million downloads and 93,258 weekly downloads at review time. This meets the officially distributed operational tool/user-documentation maturity pathway, but is not government provenance.

product_identity: NAPS2 (Not Another PDF Scanner), a cross-platform desktop document scanning and OCR application
agency: No government sponsor identified; independent project maintained by Ben Olden-Cooligan and community contributors
geography: International independent software project; no government sponsor geography established
license: GPL-2.0-or-later for the NAPS2 application; documented LGPL-2.1-or-later alternatives for SDK/Internals/Images projects and MIT for SDK samples; third-party components separate
family_note: The assigned repo is the official NAPS2 desktop application source; the current README details distinct SDK and sample-project scopes. The LICENSE file was first added to this canonical public repository in 2017; the 2009 copyright year is not treated as evidence of public-source availability. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: Active: canonical source was pushed 2026-09-28 and the first-party download page lists 8.3.2 (2026-07-22). Source, exact grants, public documentation and independent notability are sound; the decisive failure is absent government provenance. SILL presence is not used to infer authorship or funding.

decision_reason: KiTTY is a privately developed Windows SSH/telnet client and PuTTY fork. Its appearance in the French SILL is a public-sector use/recommendation lead only; no public-body creation, commissioning, funding, or stewardship of this source was found.

government_provenance.note: The first-party README describes KiTTY as a fork from PuTTY and links to the independent official project website; the source/license attributes authorship to Cyril Dupont. No government sponsor or product-specific public contribution was found. The SILL listing is not origin/provenance evidence.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the KiTTY source tree, source license, build instructions, release tags and archives; the first-party README points users to the project's own documentation/download site. It is not a source inventory mirror.

eligible_license.note: The root licence text grants standard MIT rights for KiTTY first-party code and documentation, with copyright notice/permission-preservation conditions. Code inherited from PuTTY and bundled third-party libraries keep their respective file/component terms; this review does not extend the root MIT label over those separate works.

primary_evidence.note: The official source owner published v0.76.1.13 on 2023-09-17 with release artifacts and source; the README gives build instructions and points to the official documentation/download website at https://www.9bis.net/kitty/. This is independently distributed utility software with user/build docs, while the separate SILL listing does not establish government provenance.

product_identity: KiTTY, Cyril Dupont's Windows SSH/telnet client and PuTTY-derived application, not the unrelated kitty terminal emulator
agency: No government sponsor identified; independent project by Cyril Dupont and contributors
geography: International independent software project; no government sponsor geography established
license: MIT-style grant for KiTTY first-party code; inherited PuTTY source and bundled components retain separate terms
family_note: The assigned repository is KiTTY (Windows SSH client), not kovidgoyal/kitty (GPU terminal emulator). Root LICENCE.TXT was present in the first canonical GitHub commit (2018-10-24); its 2007–2013 copyright range is not itself proof of public-release year. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: The latest official version observed is v0.76.1.13 (2023-09-17); the repo is quieter than the normal 24-month path, but the official source/release and documentation remain available. Review rejects for absent product-specific public provenance; SILL metadata was treated only as a use lead.
